title: Worker contract v1
description: Every request and response body of the worker contract, and every event on the stream. Workers execute; they do not decide. Transport and endpoints are in openapi.yaml, the rationale in ADR-0007, the prose in README.md. Shared concepts are referenced from contracts/shared/v1 and never redefined here.

AssignmentId.title: AssignmentId
AssignmentId.description: Chosen by the control plane, prefixed asg_.

StepId.title: StepId
StepId.description: The worker's own identifier for one of its steps. Stable across a resume.

CheckpointRef.title: CheckpointRef
CheckpointRef.description: An opaque reference the worker can resume from. Its format belongs to the worker.

Host.title: Host
Host.description: A host the frame allows, as a lowercase host name or an IPv4 address, optionally with a port. No wildcard: least privilege names what is allowed.

ConsumptionKind.title: ConsumptionKind
ConsumptionKind.description: What kind of limit applies to this worker's use. currency: paid per use. quota: a subscription window that blocks when exhausted. compute: held hardware in a resource class.

LimitKind.title: LimitKind
LimitKind.description: The consumption kind of one ceiling in limits: the kinds of ConsumptionKind, and tokens, the language-model tokens that consumption.reported carries as tokens_in and tokens_out. An assignment.finished that ends stopped because a running total would cross a ceiling names its kind.

Outcome.title: Outcome
Outcome.description: How an assignment ended. rejected means it never started, because the estimate did not fit the limits or the frame could not be honoured.

Capabilities.title: Capabilities
Capabilities.description: Response of GET /v1/capabilities. What this worker can do, how its use is limited, and what it supports. Capabilities are named by function, never by product. step_boundary_signal, streaming_events and estimate are constant true: without them the worker cannot satisfy sections 4, 5 and 6 of the README; they are declared so that a reader sees the obligation. A worker that declares its version has that version recorded in the provenance of every result it produces (contracts/shared/v1/Provenance.json).

version.description: The worker's own version, as it names it. Optional; recorded in provenance where present. Never a product name where the capabilities are not either.

window_seconds.description: Length of the subscription window. Required with kind quota.

unit.description: Name of the quota unit the worker reports in. Required with kind quota.

resource_classes.description: Resource classes the worker can report compute in. Required with kind compute.

currencies.description: ISO 4217 codes, lowercase, the worker can report cost in. Required with kind currency.

native_pause.description: Whether the worker can pause inside a step. Refines granularity; never required.

steering.description: Whether the worker accepts a message to a running assignment at POST /v1/assignments/{id}/messages and receives it at its next step boundary (README §6, check W-19, ADR-0139). Absent means false: the worker refuses a message.

handover.description: Whether the worker hands an assignment over at POST /v1/assignments/{id}/handover: it stops at the next step boundary and leaves a handover.state artifact another worker or a person can continue from (README §6, check W-20, ADR-0139). Absent means false: the worker refuses a handover.

Task.title: Task
Task.description: What the worker is to achieve and how it will know it is done.

acceptance.description: Criteria the result must meet, each checkable.

inputs.description: Structured inputs. Shape belongs to the task; never a credential.

BeforeCommand.title: BeforeCommand
BeforeCommand.description: A command the worker runs in its prepared workspace before the work starts, as the first step of the assignment: what makes the workspace able to run its own checks, such as installing the project's dependencies. What it writes to its standard output and its error output becomes the artifact named by `artifact`, whether it succeeds or not. A command that exits with anything but 0 fails the assignment, and the work does not start. The command is a program and its arguments, run without a shell, and it is given no credential. It reaches the network only as far as the frame's allowed_hosts reach (README §3, check W-18).

command.description: The program and its arguments, run in the workspace without a shell.

artifact.description: The artifact_id under which the command's output is published.

AfterCommand.title: AfterCommand
AfterCommand.description: A command the worker runs in its workspace once the work is done, as the last step of the assignment. Its standard output becomes the artifact named by `artifact`, byte for byte. A command that exits with anything but 0 fails the assignment, and the artifact is not produced. The command is a program and its arguments, run without a shell, and it is given no credential (README §3, check W-18).

command.description: The program and its arguments, run in the workspace without a shell.

artifact.description: The artifact_id under which the command's standard output is published.

Workspace.title: Workspace
Workspace.description: Where the worker works. For git, ref names the branch or commit and location the repository; the execution adapter may have provisioned it already, in which case location is absent.

location.description: Repository URL or path. Carries no credential.

Context.title: Context
Context.description: What the worker starts from. checkpoint_ref is present when the assignment resumes an earlier one; the worker continues after that checkpoint and produces no artifact it produced before it. handover is present when the assignment continues one that was handed over, possibly by another instance or another worker: the worker continues from the document, repeats no step it lists as done and produces no artifact it lists (W-20). Never both.

Frame.title: Frame
Frame.description: The ceiling, not a suggestion. The worker receives only the tools in allowed_tools and reaches only the hosts in allowed_hosts; both are affirmative lists, and everything outside them is refused.

allowed_hosts.description: The hosts the worker may reach over the network, and nothing else: an explicit list, never a pattern. Absent or empty means no outbound access at all, which is the default for most work. A host outside the list is refused, and the refusal is a tool.called event with host and refused true.

Limits.title: Limits
Limits.description: What the assignment may consume, per consumption kind: the worker's hard ceiling, which the control plane sets to what it reserved for the assignment. At least one kind. Checked against the estimate before the first step (W-10). While the assignment runs, a step does not start when the running total reported so far plus that step's expected demand would exceed a limit: the worker halts at the boundary it is at and ends stopped, naming the limit (W-14). tokens holds the same quantities as tokens_in and tokens_out in consumption.reported.

tokens.description: Language-model tokens, input and output apart, as consumption.reported counts them in tokens_in and tokens_out. At least one of the two.

CredentialReference.title: CredentialReference
CredentialReference.description: A secret by name only. The execution adapter injects the value into the worker's environment at runtime; the value never travels through this contract, never appears in an event, an artifact or a log, and is never stored by the worker.

path.description: Where the file is mounted. Only with injected_as file.

Callback.title: Callback
Callback.description: How the control plane receives events. v1 knows Server-Sent Events only.

EstimateRequest.title: EstimateRequest
EstimateRequest.description: Body of POST /v1/estimate: the assignment without credentials and callback. An estimate needs no secret.

Estimate.title: Estimate
Estimate.description: Response of POST /v1/estimate. May be rough; must exist. confidence low is a valid answer. The quantities are those of the shared Consumption schema; a worker that uses none of them still states steps and wall_seconds.

Estimator.title: Estimator
Estimator.description: How the worker's estimate follows from an estimate request without asking the worker (README §2, ADR-0115). Optional. fixed: every assignment is estimated as estimate. per_item: each once for every item of the list task.inputs[input], and otherwise where the task carries no such list or an empty one; every quantity, wall_seconds and steps are multiplied by the number of items. A launched worker is estimated by its estimator alone, so that no unit starts before admission; one that declares none has its worker steps refused for want of an estimate. A worker reached by endpoint is still asked at POST /v1/estimate. What an estimator yields is never below the worker's own answer for the same request (W-02).

AssignmentState.title: AssignmentState
AssignmentState.description: Response of POST /v1/assignments, GET /v1/assignments/{id}, POST /v1/assignments/{id}/stop, POST /v1/assignments/{id}/messages and POST /v1/assignments/{id}/handover. last_seq is the highest event sequence number emitted so far; 0 before the first event.

StopRequest.title: StopRequest
StopRequest.description: Body of POST /v1/assignments/{id}/stop. The stop takes effect at the next step boundary. ceiling_seconds bounds how long the running step may still take; absent means the worker's own ceiling.

MessageId.title: MessageId
MessageId.description: Chosen by the control plane, prefixed msg_. A message posted again under the same id is received once.

SteeringMessage.title: SteeringMessage
SteeringMessage.description: Body of POST /v1/assignments/{id}/messages: a message to a running assignment. The worker receives it at its next step boundary, reports message.received once, and the steps after that boundary have it as an input of their work. It is an input like the task's inputs: it cannot widen the frame, raise a limit or move the deadline (README §6, W-19).

HandoverRequest.title: HandoverRequest
HandoverRequest.description: Body of POST /v1/assignments/{id}/handover. The handover takes effect at the next step boundary, as a stop does; ceiling_seconds bounds how long the running step may still take. The worker then produces the handover.state artifact and ends stopped, naming it (README §6, W-20).

HandoverStep.title: HandoverStep
HandoverStep.description: One step of the worker's own plan that was done when the assignment was handed over.

Handover.title: Handover
Handover.description: The content of a handover.state artifact: an assignment handed over at a step boundary, as a document that stands on its own. summary, steps and artifacts are for a person, who can continue the work from them; what the work changed in its workspace is among the artifacts. resume is the worker's own: a worker of the same kind continues from it without anything the first instance kept. A new assignment carries the document in context.handover; it repeats no step listed here and produces no artifact listed here (W-20).

summary.description: For a person: what was done and what remains.

artifacts.description: Every artifact the assignment, and every assignment it continued, produced before the handover; the handover.state artifact itself is not among them.

messages.description: The steering messages received before the handover.

resume.description: The worker's own, opaque to everyone else: what a worker of the same kind needs to continue. Never a credential.

RelayRequest.title: RelayRequest
RelayRequest.description: The outbound binding (README §8, ADR-0139): what POST <base>/next answers a worker that connects to a host instead of listening. One request of this contract, which the worker handles as if it had arrived at its endpoint and answers at POST <base>/answers/{request_id}: the header Relay-Status carries the status code, Content-Type the type, and the body the answer's body, streamed while it lasts. Every request is answered exactly once (W-21).

path.description: The path of the contract's endpoint, with its query, as a request at the worker's endpoint would carry it.

headers.description: Of the request's headers, those the contract gives a meaning.

body.description: The request's body as text; absent when it has none.

ArtifactList.title: ArtifactList
ArtifactList.description: Response of GET /v1/assignments/{id}/artifacts. Each artifact's uri says where its bytes are; by default GET /v1/assignments/{id}/artifacts/{artifact_id} on the worker.

Health.title: Health
Health.description: Response of GET /v1/health. Readiness, not liveness: ready means the worker can accept an assignment now.

EventBase.title: EventBase
EventBase.description: What every event carries. seq starts at 1 and increases by exactly 1; the stream is resumable from any seq.

ReachStated.title: ReachStated
ReachStated.description: What the worker put within reach of this assignment's work, stated once, before the first step.started. tools names every capability a call of this assignment can be made under, refused or not: a capability not named cannot be called at all. hosts, when present, names every host a call of this assignment can name: a host not named cannot be reached at all; absent, the worker bounds the hosts only at the moment of a call. A tool.called outside the statement makes it false. The statement is optional: a worker that offers its work every tool and refuses at the call states nothing. It lets the conformance suite see a tool or a host taken out of the frame as not offered, where no call to it was attempted (W-07, W-13).

StepStarted.title: StepStarted
StepStarted.description: A step of the worker's own plan begins. kind names the class of work in one lowercase token: plan, edit, test, shell, epoch, evaluate.

StepProgress.title: StepProgress
StepProgress.description: Progress inside a step. progress is for work measured in units, such as epochs.

ToolCalled.title: ToolCalled
ToolCalled.description: The worker used, or refused to use, a tool. Arguments travel as a digest, never in clear. A tool outside the frame's allowed_tools is refused, and so is a host outside the frame's allowed_hosts; the refusal is this event with refused true. effect says whether the call acts outside the workspace.

host.description: The host the call reaches over the network, when it reaches one. A host outside the frame's allowed_hosts is refused.

effect.description: What the call acts on, where the worker says so. local: nothing outside the assignment's workspace changes — a read, an edit of the workspace's files, a test run. outward: something outside it changes, such as a record written or a message delivered. Absent says nothing (ADR-0139 §5).

DecisionMade.title: DecisionMade
DecisionMade.description: The worker chose a path. rationale says why. This is an execution choice within the frame, not a decision request; those are raised by the control plane.

ConsumptionReported.title: ConsumptionReported
ConsumptionReported.description: What one step used. Emitted per step, not at the end; without it there is no admission control. At least one quantity.

StepBoundary.title: StepBoundary
StepBoundary.description: The step's result is persisted and the worker could stop here. The promise that at most one step of work is lost. A stop takes effect at this point.

ArtifactProduced.title: ArtifactProduced
ArtifactProduced.description: A result exists. The same artifact appears in GET /v1/assignments/{id}/artifacts. A resumed assignment never re-emits an artifact produced before its checkpoint.

MessageReceived.title: MessageReceived
MessageReceived.description: A steering message was received, at a step boundary: after the step that was running reached its boundary, or before the first step, and never inside a step. step_id names the step whose boundary it was. Emitted once per message; the steps after it have the message as an input (W-19).

ModelCalled.title: ModelCalled
ModelCalled.description: The worker received an answer of a language model inside a step. Reported once per answer, so that the tool calls between two answers can be seen (ADR-0139 §5, ADR-0132). Optional: a worker that uses no model emits none.

AssignmentFinished.title: AssignmentFinished
AssignmentFinished.description: The last event of a stream. stopped carries the checkpoint to resume from; failed and rejected carry a reason. limit names the kind of the ceiling in limits that halted the assignment: only with stopped, and never for a stop requested through POST /stop. handover names the handover.state artifact of an assignment handed over: only with stopped.

limit.description: The kind of the ceiling whose running total halted the assignment at a step boundary (W-14). Absent when the stop was requested, and when the worker stopped on its own before its unit's wall clock (TAKTUS_UNIT_WALL_SECONDS, ADR-0102).

handover.description: The artifact_id of the handover.state artifact, when the assignment was handed over (W-20). Only with stopped.

Event.title: Event
Event.description: One message on GET /v1/assignments/{id}/events. On the wire: the SSE id field carries seq, the SSE event field carries type, the SSE data field carries this object as one line of JSON.

Transcript.title: Transcript
Transcript.description: Not a wire object. The fixture shape for the conformance suite: one assignment, the estimate the worker gave for it, every event of its stream in order, the steering messages the suite posted with the last seq the worker's answer to each named, and whether a handover was requested. The suite checks the stream rules W-03 to W-07, W-10, W-11, W-13, W-14, W-18, W-19 and W-20 against this shape.

accepted_at_seq.description: last_seq of the state the worker answered the message with.

CapacityProbe.title: CapacityProbe
CapacityProbe.description: Not a wire object. The fixture shape for check W-15: the places the worker declares, the states of the assignments the suite held, read after the answer, the answer to one more assignment, and the status a lookup of that assignment returned after a 503. The suite checks the capacity rule against this shape.

UnknownIdProbe.title: UnknownIdProbe
UnknownIdProbe.description: Not a wire object. The fixture shape for check W-16: an assignment id the worker never received, and the answer to GET /v1/assignments/{id} for it. The suite checks the unknown-id rule against this shape.

RepeatedIdProbe.title: RepeatedIdProbe
RepeatedIdProbe.description: Not a wire object. The fixture shape for check W-17: the state of an assignment the worker held, read before the suite posted its id again, the answer to that repeated POST /v1/assignments, and the state of the id read after it. The suite checks the repeated-id rule against this shape.

RelayProbe.title: RelayProbe
RelayProbe.description: Not a wire object. The fixture shape for check W-21: the requests a host relayed to a worker connected over the outbound binding, and every answer the worker posted, in order, with the Relay-Status it carried (null where it carried none or one that is no status code). The suite checks the binding rule against this shape.
